headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared project files; no direct evidence of tighter coupling, so other risks stay lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a per-project directory and has no self-isolation by default, while nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. If the pair shares the project directory, A can place instruction-like content that B may ingest. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF B reads A-authored files as trusted input without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Add a provenance header check before B consumes files
Disable automatic file ingestion for B
Review any A-generated prompt files before B runs
requires-engineering: add workspace-level isolation or locking

B_data_leakage.rationale: A reads and writes the project directory and can call configured model APIs; B has allowlisted network egress but no documented local-only boundary. If sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace, A can expose them through model calls or outputs, and B may also transmit context externally. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in the shared project directory
IF either agent forwards file contents or context to an external model/API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a redacted copy of inputs for both agents
Restrict outbound network destinations
Audit what files each agent reads before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but it does not modify git state; B has no documented write or git capabilities. The profiles show overlap on network egress only, which is not a mutable-resource conflict. Without shared write scopes or locking issues, capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF B is later granted write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource
mitigations: Keep B read-only
Avoid concurrent writes to the same workspace
Run A and B in separate sandboxes
Document ownership of any shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces generated code and writes files; B is a scientific-research agent with no documented verification or critique workflow. If B consumes A's outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream reasoning or actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated files or claims as source material
IF B does not independently verify A's outputs before acting
mitigations: Require B to cite independent sources
Insert a human review step before downstream use
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Compare A outputs against tests or checksums
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly handles generated source code and OPENAI_API_KEY, while B has no documented data classes or residency/compliance commitments. There is no evidence of a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. The other agent is not cited because B lacks documented compliance-sensitive handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into A's project directory
IF B is expected to process the same regulated data without documented controls
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in A's workspace
Confirm B's retention and residency settings before use
Use synthetic or masked data
Record a data-class policy for the pair
